required_evidence: Construct an algebraic obstruction from a linear splitting and prove that its class is independent of that splitting.
Prove both implications between vanishing of the obstruction and existence of a G-equivariant linear splitting under the given field hypothesis.
Describe the entire nonempty space of equivariant splittings and prove naturality under isomorphisms of the short exact sequence.
critical_errors: Average by dividing by |G| without proving that |G| is invertible in k.
Conclude unconditional equivariant splitting from finite-dimensionality or finiteness of G.
Confuse a choice-independent obstruction class with a choice-independent cocycle representative.
Assert that an existing equivariant splitting is unique among all equivariant splittings, without a valid argument excluding nonzero differences in Hom_G(C,A).

Claim that every split short exact sequence admits a preferred equivariant splitting determined solely by the sequence, independent of the supplied initial splitting, and natural under all isomorphisms of the underlying sequences.
Use Hom(C,A) with the wrong G-action so that the displayed defect does not satisfy the claimed cocycle identity.
completion_policy: Completion requires the requested choice-independent existence criterion, full freedom of solutions, and isomorphism naturality. Any equivalent construction is acceptable; group-cohomology terminology and the optional counterexamples in the reference are not mandatory. A proved construction may legitimately be canonical relative to the supplied initial splitting s; assess independence from s as a separate claim.
open_task_policy: Accept independently verified alternative constructions, counterexamples and unexpected results. Explicit conditional results are valid contributions but do not by themselves settle the original scope. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
